primitives.name: Intentional Motion Illusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: When we will to execute a movement and the movement for some reason does not occur, unless the sensation of the part's NoT moving is a strong one, we are apt to fel as if the movement had actually taken place.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I': 'dimensionless intent strength', 'M': 'dimensionless motor activation', 'S': 'dimensionless sensory feedback'}
primitives.assumptions: Motor intention (I) triggers perceived motion (M) even when actual motion (M_actual) is zero due to sensory suppression.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S < threshold, perception of M becomes dominant over actual M_actual.

layer2.mapping: GSI's Bayesian update on I vs. M_actual mirrors GSE's state transition from commanded to perceived motion under constraint.
layer2.telemetry: Subjective motion report vs. objective kinematic tracking.

primitives.name: Anesthetic Movement Delusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Close the patient's eyes, hold his anæsthetic arm still, and tell him to raise his hand to his head; and when he opens his eyes he will be astonished to find that the movement has not taken place.
primitives.assumptions: In anesthetic state (A=1), P ≠ R due to disrupted sensory-motor loop.
primitives.breakdown_regime: A = 1 ⇒ P = 1, R = 0, violating causal consistency.

layer2.mapping: GSE's perceptual kernel maps P to R via sensory gating; GSI's probabilistic model assigns P as evidence for R despite absence of physical change.
layer2.telemetry: Discrepancy between reported and observed motion in anesthetized subjects.

primitives.name: Sternberg Intention Equivalence
primitives.verbatim_quote: Sternberg who wrote on the subject in 1885,\ lays it down as a law that the intention to move is the same thing as the feeling of the motion.
primitives.assumptions: J ≡ F under normal conditions; however, this equivalence breaks under sensory constraint.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sensory input is suppressed, J ≠ F, leading to hallucination.

layer2.mapping: GSI's belief function equates J and F; GSE's action model treats J as control signal, F as feedback, both misaligned under constraint.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between self-reported intention and actual motor output.

In GSI, this manifests as a Bayesian belief update where prior expectation of motion overrides posterior sensory evidence. The GSE interprets this through a state transition model where the system assumes motion has occurred based on internal command signals. The anesthetic movement delusion exemplifies a failure mode in sensory-motor integration, where the absence of tactile feedback leads to a perceptual error. This is modeled as a conditional probability P(M|A=1) = 1, while P(R|A=1) = 0. The Sternberg equivalence principle posits that intention and sensation are identical, but this breaks down under sensory suppression. In GSI, this creates a cognitive dissonance in belief propagation; in GSE, it results in a faulty control loop where the system believes motion has occurred without physical evidence.
